$mirrors: docs/cultural_data_inventory_catalog.json (cultural G.0 mirror of lexical A.0)
$catalog_intent: This catalog is a pre-ingest blueprint. It enumerates the in-scope historical sources, their procurement parameters, expected corpus envelopes, and explicit deadends, as verified by the six recon agents on 2026-05-31 against actual upstream artifacts (recon outputs at tmp/pipeline4_recon/<source>/recon.json). It does NOT yet carry sampling_stride_proof or per-field sample_indices because no fixtures have been captured. Those are added in a separate architect-caste commit after Pipeline 4 adapters land under ingest/historical/ and cached fixtures are persisted under tests/historical/fixtures/. The H.0 phase exists so the procurement-completeness rule (H1) has a stable contract to verify against once Pipeline 4 is wired.

scope.pipeline: Pipeline 4 historical attestation (sidecar; air-gapped from Pipeline 2 lexical; shares physical infrastructure with cultural Docker stack but uses disjoint Neo4j labels and a separate Qdrant collection hist_col)

explicit_deadends.name: Talmud-Bavli
explicit_deadends.reason: William Davidson Edition English is CC-BY-NC 4.0; Wikisource Bavli Hebrew is CC-BY-SA 4.0 (viral). Volume (~49,000 chunks) is also large enough to dilute v1 retrieval signal. Deferred to v2.

explicit_deadends.name: Talmud-Yerushalmi
explicit_deadends.reason: Mechon-Mamre and Venice Edition Hebrew ship with license=unknown in Sefaria export JSON. Guggenheimer English is CC-BY but pairing it with license-unknown Hebrew is not a clean v1 commitment. Deferred to v2.

explicit_deadends.name: OCP-source-language-witnesses
explicit_deadends.reason: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha (pseudepigrapha.org) serves source-language text only via web2py AJAX which returns HTTP 500 to direct curl. Ethiopic 1 Enoch, Syriac 2 Baruch, Latin 4 Ezra, Greek Testaments-12 and Psalms of Solomon are reachable only via browser scrape or by contacting Ian W. Scott. Out of v1 scope.

explicit_deadends.name: Philo-Cohn-Wendland-Greek
explicit_deadends.reason: PerseusDL canonical-greekLit does not contain Philo (tlg0018 is absent; verified directory listing shows tlg0016/0017/0019 with no tlg0018). No clean-license machine-readable Cohn-Wendland Greek edition was located. Philo ingest is English-only (Yonge 1854) in v1.

explicit_deadends.name: IAA-Leon-Levy-DSS-images
explicit_deadends.reason: Israel Antiquities Authority terms of use forbid reproduction or distribution; single-copy private use only. Images cannot be machine-ingested. Link-out reference under the single-copy-private-use clause is acceptable but no data ingest.

explicit_deadends.name: Wise-Abegg-Cook-DSS-English
explicit_deadends.reason: Commercial copyright (HarperSanFrancisco/HarperOne). Vermes, Charlesworth, Garcia Martinez are likewise commercial. No clean-license complete English DSS translation exists. DSS v1 uses original-language ETCBC transliteration only per Option A discipline; English meaning is rendered at Pipeline 3 synthesis time by Opus 4.7.

explicit_deadends.name: Scripta-Qumranica-Electronica
explicit_deadends.reason: Joint Goettingen/Haifa/TAU/IAA platform. Promising mid-term but no published bulk download or stable API at probe time. Revisit when SQE publishes its open dataset.

explicit_deadends.name: Sibylline-Oracles-Christian-recensions
explicit_deadends.reason: Charles 1913 deliberately includes only the Jewish strata (books III, IV, V plus fragments). Books I-II, VI-VIII, XI-XIV are Christian recensions (second-to-fourth century CE) outside the canonical Charles selection. Out of v1 scope; would belong to a future patristic-extension layer if scope expands.

sampling_method.phase_note: sampling_stride_proof and per-field sample_indices are NOT populated in H.0. They are added in H.1 after Pipeline 4 adapters land and fixtures are captured under tests/historical/fixtures/. The H.1 commit is architect-caste with a [SCHEMA-REVISION] tag if any expected_counts or live_corpus_bound values move.

historical_vs_cultural_note: The cultural layer surfaces denominational and confessional INTERPRETATIONS of Scripture (how each tradition reads a passage). The historical layer surfaces extra-biblical ATTESTATION of the world around Scripture (what Jewish historians, Roman officials, second-temple-period writers, rabbinic teachers, and Qumran scribes recorded). The two layers share the cultural Docker stack and the :Doctrine and :Question nodes but use disjoint chunk labels (CulturalChunk via ADDRESSES vs HistoricalChunk via ATTESTS) and disjoint Qdrant collections (cult_col vs hist_col). Pipeline 3 synthesis reads both as separate diagnostic blocks; neither overrides the Pipeline 2 lexical verdict.

sources.name: Josephus-Perseus
sources.license_evidence: Inline <licence target='https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/'> in all eight teiHeader/fileDesc/publicationStmt/availability blocks, plus repo top-level license.md. Verified in tmp/pipeline4_recon/josephus/recon.json.
sources.redistribute_note: Sidecar JSON inherits ShareAlike obligation; a per-file LICENSE notice is mandatory in historical/ output.
sources.anchor_pattern: josephus.<work>.<book>.<niese_section> where <work> in {ant, vita, apion, wars}
required_flags: contested-interpolation: Antiquities 18.63 (Testimonium Flavianum); type=partial-interpolation; redact_for_embedding=true on the 'He was [the] Christ' clause
editor-overlay: <note resp='editor'> elements are 19th-century Whiston commentary, NOT Josephus; extract into chunk['whiston_editor_notes'] separately, never inline
sources.format: TEI P5 EpiDoc XML, UTF-8, polytonic Greek Unicode in grc2

sources.name: Philo-Yonge
sources.license_evidence: Yonge 1854 translation, translator died 1891; pre-1923 US PD. earlychristianwritings.com index.html verbatim notice: 'This work has been transcribed by anonymous from the 1993 reprint, but it remains the translation of C. D. Yonge, which is public domain.' Archive.org metadata: Public Domain Mark 1.0. Verified in tmp/pipeline4_recon/philo/recon.json.
sources.fetch_constraint: ModSecurity blocks default curl UA; fixed Chrome User-Agent required on every request; throttle 1 req/sec.
sources.live_corpus_bound_reconciliation: The H.0 recon estimate of ~13000 was a paragraph overcount. The faithful full ingest of all 45 Yonge treatises yields 8405 Cohn-Wendland paragraphs (verified by independent paragraph-marker count ~8414). Bound moved to bracket the faithful actual; no data is missing.
required_flags: provenance: QG books 41-43 and De Providentia 38-39 are armenian-via-latin via yonge-english; loss_status=partial; mark provenance.witness_chain explicitly
editor-overlay: {*} and {**...} inline footnote markers are Yonge editorial; extract to chunk['yonge_footnotes'] separately
sources.format: HTML 4.01 with iso-8859-1 declared encoding; ASCII prose with rare Greek single-character entities; JS Greek-font conversion block at tail of every page must be stripped before parsing

sources.name: Pseudepigrapha-Charles-1913
sources.license_evidence: Charles 1913 APOT volume II; author died 1931; published 1913; US PD pre-1929 cutoff. Verified across CCEL, sacred-texts BOE (1917 reprint), earlychristianwritings, Wikisource APOT vol II. Verified in tmp/pipeline4_recon/pseudepigrapha/recon.json.

upstream_urls_per_work.1enoch_primary: https://sacred-texts.com/bib/boe/ (boe004.htm..boe112.htm, one chapter per file, UTF-8 declared, ceiling-bracket apparatus preserved)
upstream_urls_per_work.test12: https://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/patriarchs-charles.html (single page, all 12 testaments, bold chapter, inline verse digits)
upstream_urls_per_work.sibor: same Wikisource volume; Lanchester translation; books III, IV, V plus fragments only

sources.live_corpus_bound_reconciliation: Four of seven works ingested in v1 from clean public-domain Charles-1913 transcriptions (1 Enoch per-verse from sacred-texts BOE; Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs per-chapter recension-flagged; Jubilees per-chapter; Sibylline Oracles per-strophe, Jewish strata only). 2 Baruch, 4 Ezra, and Psalms of Solomon are deferred: Wikisource APOT Volume II transcribes only the Sibylline Oracles, and the standalone Wikisource Psalms of Solomon is a community translation, not the PD Charles text. They are obtainable from CCEL Charles APOT in a later procurement pass; SOURCE_SLUGS still declares all seven so they drop in without code change. 4 Ezra is never double-counted against 2 Esdras.
required_flags: contested-interpolation: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs is a Christianized recension; type=recension-layer; note must cite Charles introductions for Jewish-vs-Christian stratum identification
cross-link: 1enoch.1.9 must link Jude.1.14-15 as composite-tradition witness
cross-link: 4ezra (Charles) is the same work as 2 Esdras 3-14 in Vulgate/KJV apocrypha; avoid double-count
sources.format: HTML mixed (CCEL legacy HTML 4.0 with windows-1252; sacred-texts modern HTML UTF-8 with U+2308/U+2309 ceiling-bracket apparatus; earlychristianwritings UTF-8; Wikisource UTF-8 per-page)

sources.name: Tacitus-Annals-Perseus
sources.license_evidence: Repo license.md states CC-BY-SA-4.0; underlying Fisher 1906 Latin and Church/Brodribb 1869 English are PD by age. Verified in tmp/pipeline4_recon/roman-historians/recon.json.
sources.root_path: ingest/historical/roman_historians.py (module A: TEI P4 milestone slicer)

required_flags: text-critical-variant: Annals 15.44 'Christianos vs Chrestianos' in Mediceus II; contested_interpolation.type=text-critical-variant; note must cite Fisher 1906 against Koestermann/Heubner
loss_status: partial; Annals books 7-10 and second half of book 16 are lost in antiquity
sources.format: TEI P4 SGML-ish XML; div1[@type=book] + empty <milestone unit='chapter'/> markers; chapter-text extraction must slice between consecutive milestones, NOT by ancestry

sources.name: Suetonius-Twelve-Caesars-Perseus
sources.root_path: ingest/historical/roman_historians.py (module B: TEI P5 EpiDoc nested-div walker)
sources.scope_recommendation: christian-relevant-only (Claudius 25.3, 25.4, 25.5; Nero 16.1, 16.2, 16.3) for v1; defer full Twelve Caesars
sources.scope_reconciliation: The Ihm Teubner edition in the Perseus EpiDoc file splits Nero chapter 16 into sections 1 and 2 only; there is no 16.3 to extract. The Christian notice (afflicti suppliciis Christiani) falls in Nero 16.2, which is captured. Christian-relevant Latin chunks: Claudius 25.3/25.4/25.5 and Nero 16.1/16.2, total 5.
sources.format: TEI P5 EpiDoc nested <div type='textpart' n='N' subtype='chapter'> > <div n='M' subtype='section'>; chapter-text IS the wrapper subtree

sources.root_path: ingest/historical/roman_historians.py (module B: TEI P5 EpiDoc nested-div walker)
sources.language_gap: Latin only in this repo. English requires the separate Pliny-Letters-Melmoth-Wikisource adapter.

sources.name: Pliny-Letters-Melmoth-Wikisource

sources.name: Mishnah-Sefaria
sources.license_evidence: Hebrew via Torat Emet 357 (Public Domain) or Vilna 1913 (Public Domain). English primary via Joshua Kulp's Mishnah Yomit (CC-BY). English fallback via Sefaria Community Translation (CC0). Per-tractate license fields verified in Sefaria-Export JSON metadata. Verified in tmp/pipeline4_recon/sefaria/recon.json.
sources.upstream_url: gs://sefaria-export/json/Mishnah/ (Sefaria-Export is now a thin index repo; actual texts live in the public GCS bucket)
sources.tractate_name_convention: Sefaria English transliteration (Berakhot, Sanhedrin, Pesachim, etc.); stable across the export
required_flags: inline-html: <i>, <strong>, <big>, <i data-overlay='Vilna Pages'> tags must be stripped before embedding; overlay data-value captured into chunk metadata.printed_page
tractate-normalization: Pirkei Avot files under 'Pirkei Avot' not 'Mishnah Avot'
version-pinning: must pick one canonical version per tractate per language; document choice in chunk metadata.version_title
sources.format: JSON depth-2 nested arrays text[chapter_idx][mishnah_idx]; UTF-8; Hebrew Torat Emet 357 carries full nikkud

sources.name: DSS-ETCBC
sources.license_evidence: Verbatim '@license=Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License' header in every .tf data file. Code is MIT; data is CC-BY-NC. Per docs/about.md: 'Martin Abegg graciously gave permission to Jarod Jacobs to use his data and to distribute the results under a CC-BY-NC license.' Verified in tmp/pipeline4_recon/dss/recon.json.
sources.redistribute_reason: NC clause blocks commercial redistribution. Local storage and personal query are fine. Engine code is published under MIT/Apache; the DSS data is NOT re-shipped via the public engine repo. Per-chunk redistribute=false enforces this at the license_guard layer.
sources.english_translation_discipline: Option A locked. text and text_to_embed both carry the ETCBC transliteration verbatim. No engine-authored English gloss is pre-baked. Pipeline 3 synthesis renders English meaning per query via Opus 4.7.
sources.biblical_scroll_coverage: 1QIsa-a, 1QIsa-b, 4QSam-a/b/c, 11QPs-a, 4QDeut variants, MasPs-a, etc. (biblical=1 feature flag in tf)
sources.live_corpus_bound_reconciliation: The H.0 recon estimate of ~9800 badly undercounted: it reflected a marquee-only mental model. The faithful full ETCBC corpus has 52895 line nodes, of which 49178 form a valid cave-Q anchor and are ingested (caves 1 through 11, including 11Q19 Temple Scroll). 3643 lines across 78 scrolls are genuinely unrepresentable as cave-Q anchors (PAM museum-plate sigla, Wadi Murabbaat Mur, Masada Mas, Cairo Damascus CD which has no cave-Q form, and slash sigla like 5/6Hev); these are skipped honestly, never force-fit. All sources are kept in full; retrieval balance across source types is enforced at the Pipeline 4 context-builder layer (PER_TYPE_LIMIT), not by trimming ingest.
required_flags: redistribute=false at chunk level; license_guard enforces no bulk export

transliteration-conventions: ETCBC bracket flags must be preserved as metadata: [ ] reconstruction, [[ ]] vacat, { } scribal deletion, ( ) alternate, < > suggested correction, ! ! uncertain letter, & damaged letter, # uncertain trace
Option A discipline: text_to_embed == text; no engine-authored gloss in v1
sources.format: Text-Fabric .tf files (Apache TF v11.x) plus parallel glyph.tf for Unicode Hebrew; ETCBC transliteration is Latin transliteration of Hebrew/Aramaic
sources.recon_verdict_reasoning: Real and reachable, with all marquee scrolls covered. YELLOW because (1) CC-BY-NC is a hard blocker for any future commercial release, and (2) no clean-license English exists for sectarian DSS, so English rendering relies on Option A query-time synthesis quality.

post_ingest_obligations.h1_procurement_completeness: Every source listed in scope.in_scope_historical must have a corresponding ingest/historical/<slug>.py adapter that passes its dedicated test suite under tests/historical/. Every entry in scope.explicit_deadends must carry a deadend_evidence URL plus a committed user approval in this catalog.
post_ingest_obligations.h4_count_contract: Once Pipeline 4 has run end-to-end, the per-source chunk counts must fall within live_corpus_bound. Drift outside the bound triggers an architect-caste [SCHEMA-REVISION] commit moving the bound, never a silent acceptance.
post_ingest_obligations.h5_snapshot_determinism: Two consecutive ingest runs over identical inputs must produce identical chunk_id sets per source. Pipeline 4 attestation outputs (historical/<id>.json) need not be byte-identical (LLM judgment) but must pass the schema's triangle test (attestation_type and confidence within +/- 0.05).
post_ingest_obligations.h6_adapter_purity: All ingest/historical/ adapters must be pure: no subprocess, no socket, no httpx/requests/urllib/aiohttp, no dynamic import, no non-data/private path literals. Fetch is a Pipeline 1 procurement step run separately by the orchestrator; adapters parse local files only.
post_ingest_obligations.fixture_capture: tests/historical/fixtures/ must persist a cached copy of every upstream artifact the adapters were captured against. Per-adapter fixture_paths_planned must become fixture_paths once captured.
